root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation build compiles src/plugins/template/tests/functional (ov_template_func_tests) with CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31 on a self-hosted Windows runner. Several heavily templated op_reference test translation units (col2im.cpp, cum_sum.cpp, ctc_greedy_decoder.cpp, cosh.cpp) instantiate many std:: template specializations, driving per-cl.exe-process memory usage very high. With 31 parallel MSVC compiler processes plus ccache overhead, the runner's available memory is exhausted, so individual cl.exe invocations throw std::bad_alloc or hit fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and ninja aborts the build. This is a recurring infrastructure/resource-contention issue (count=17 in the pattern database, most recent occurrences within the last 24 hours) rather than a code defect introduced by this specific commit; the commit under investigation (PR #39001, NPU VM runtime move) does not touch the template plugin or its tests.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside the CI self-hosted Windows runner: requires building the `ov_template_func_tests` target with `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31` (or similarly high) under memory-constrained conditions. Locally, building with a high ninja -j parallelism on a machine with limited RAM while ccache is cold can reproduce similar cl.exe out-of-heap-space failures.
recommended_actions: Lower CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL for the Windows CC Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode job (or switch to a memory-aware job pool, e.g. ninja -j via /l or RAM-based throttling) instead of a fixed high value like 31.

Investigate whether the self-hosted Windows runner pool used for this job has sufficient RAM for the current parallelism level, and consider increasing runner memory or reducing concurrent compiler jobs.
Consider splitting or simplifying heavily-templated op_reference test files (col2im.cpp, cum_sum.cpp, ctc_greedy_decoder.cpp, cosh.cpp) to reduce per-TU memory footprint during MSVC compilation.
Given this is the 17th occurrence, escalate to the CI infrastructure owners to proactively tune Windows CC build parallelism/runner sizing rather than treating each occurrence as a one-off.
prevention_strategies: Tie CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL to the runner's available RAM (e.g., jobs = min(logical_cores, RAM_GB / per-job-memory-estimate)) rather than a fixed count. Monitor MSVC/ninja build memory usage on self-hosted Windows runners and alert when nearing capacity. Track recurrence of this exact signature in the pattern database and raise a dedicated CI infra ticket once it crosses a recurrence threshold.
historical_context: This exact failure signature (Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 and linker fatal error LNK1102 under high parallelism) has now been recorded 17 times in the CI Doctor Post-Commit pattern database, first seen 2026-11-03T07:07:04Z and repeatedly recurring (including runs within the last few hours), indicating a persistent, unresolved CI infrastructure capacity issue rather than an isolated incident.
